name: exploit
cleaning_prompt: DATASET: U.S. monthly unemployment-rate panel (~1950–2024). Clean the CURRENT row month only. Adhere strictly to panel-safety rules: each row is one calendar month; clean only that month's input text. NEVER apply global year cutoffs (e.g., discard pre-2000), NEVER copy 2020s+ BLS data into historical rows, and NEVER invent or substitute data. If the source is empty/NA/whitespace or contains <~40 chars of real content, output EMPTY. DO NOT emit empty JSON objects or header-only shells. For each row, extract only U.S. national labor metrics (unemployment rate, nonfarm payrolls, jobless claims, participation, recession/jobs indicators) whose printed release year is within ±1 year of the row's calendar year. Discard any fact whose release year differs by ≥2 years from the row year. Strip all foreign, state-level, demographic, or non-labor context (e.g., poverty, inflation, minimum wage, job additions, EU comparisons, foreign unemployment data). Retain only clear, on-period U.S. national labor facts even if buried in noise. Do not remove a valid U.S. labor metric just because the same paragraph contains off-year or off-topic content—strip the noise, keep the driver. If both claims and payrolls are present, keep both. Use only BLS or equivalent official U.S. sources (e.g., BLS, Fed, Treasury) for U.S. national metrics. Non-BLS sources (e.g., digitalcommons.nyls.edu, fortune.com, epi.org, www.latimes.com) are forbidden unless they are confirmed BLS-aligned and on-period. When a non-BLS source appears, verify it is not a recycled encyclopedia block or foreign context. If the source is non-BLS and off-period, or contains unverified claims, drop it. Do not keep incomplete sentences or non-core metrics. Prioritize on-row and near-dated U.S. labor data. Output must be plain text bullets or short labeled lines (e.g., 'Unemployment rate: 3.8% (BLS, 2023-12)', 'Nonfarm payrolls: 150.2M (BLS, 2023-11)'). If no valid U.S. national labor metric remains after filtering, output EMPTY. NEVER invent a rate or value. NEVER use off-month data (e.g., March 13 in a 2020-04-20 row). DO NOT use 2024 BLS data in any pre-2023 row. If the row's source has no usable on-period U.S. labor driver, output EMPTY. Do not over-delete—keep valid U.S. national labor facts even if the source is noisy. Final output must be a plain text list of valid facts, or EMPTY.
